nodes.title: Material Breach and Constructive Conditions
nodes.conceptSummary:
### 1. Pangkal Anomali
Pemilik rumah sering berupaya membatalkan seluruh pembayaran kontrak pembangunan hanya karena pipa yang dipasang bermerek Reading Pipe Brand B bukannya Brand A, padahal kualitas fisiknya identik. Jika deviasi sepele membatalkan seluruh pembayaran, industri konstruksi akan lumpuh akibat pemerasan pembeli.

### 2. Prototipe Intuitif
Bayangkan saluran pipa air di sebuah bangunan. Jika sambungan pipa utama pecah dan merendam seluruh fondasi (material breach), katup air wajib ditutup total. Namun jika cat pipa luar sedikit berbeda merek (immaterial breach), air tetap mengalir lancar dan pemilik cukup meminta selisih harga cat kaleng.

### 3. Invarian & Operasi Inti
Invarian mutlak sistem adalah **Doktrin Pelaksanaan Substansial (Substantial Performance - Jacob & Youngs v. Kent)**: pelanggaran minor yang tidak melukai tujuan pokok kontrak tidak membatalkan kewajiban pihak lain, melainkan hanya memberikan hak klaim ganti rugi selisih nilai.

forwardPass.prompt: "Predict whether a homeowner can lawfully terminate a building contract and refuse payment if the builder used identical pipe of Brand B instead of Brand A."

options.text: Cannot terminate: under the doctrine of substantial performance (Jacob & Youngs v. Kent), an immaterial breach only entitles the owner to difference-in-value damages, not contract forfeiture.
options.causalRationale: Correct: Substantial performance prevents forfeiture for minor, immaterial variances.

options.text: Can terminate immediately because any deviation from express contract specifications constitutes a complete material breach.
options.causalRationale: Strict Condition Fallacy: Equity rejects economic forfeiture when performance is substantially complete.

options.text: Owner must pay full contract price with zero deduction because the builder acted in good faith.
options.causalRationale: Damage Entitlement Slip: Immaterial breach still entitles the non-breaching party to nominal or difference-in-value damages.

forwardPass.groundTruth: "Cannot terminate: under the doctrine of substantial performance (Jacob & Youngs v. Kent), an immaterial breach only entitles the owner to difference-in-value damages, not contract forfeiture."
